start.title: Your first dental visit
start.intro: Follow the visit from a new chart through the final record.

first.title: Open or create a patient
first.text: Use the plus button or Open an animal. Search by name or patient number before creating a patient. If the New visit chooser appears, select Dental procedure and choose Start visit. Check the patient name, species, number and visit date in Patient.

second.title: Document care as you go
second.text: Use Exam and Anesthesia for observations, Charting for tooth measurements, Diagnosis for findings, and Procedure for work performed. Add images and interpretation in Imaging. Record treatment and discharge instructions in their own sections.

third.title: Review, save, and share
third.text: Use Review and export to check the clinical chart or owner report. Use Finalize when the record is ready to close. Watch the save status in the patient tab before leaving and reopen a saved visit with Edit chart if you need to amend it.

patients.title: Patients and visit history
patients.intro: Open the right dated visit and compare earlier records.

first.title: Find a patient
first.text:
Open the patient picker with the plus button. Verify the patient number when names match. Choose an existing visit to continue it, or choose New visit and check the visit type before starting.

In Patients or Rechecks, use search and the filters above the list. If there are no matches, choose Clear filters below the results. Rechecks still shows only due visits. If the list could not load, choose Try again.

second.title: Switch visits and patient tabs
second.text: The tab shows the patient, visit date and type. Use the visit switcher to open another saved visit. Two visits on the same date can have different types. Closing a tab keeps the patient and their visits in the workspace history.

third.title: Review earlier records
third.text: In Patient, choose View visit history when prior visits are available. Select the date and type, then review the note or export that visit. Use the visit switcher to reopen a visit for editing.

charting.title: Charting, diagnosis, and procedures
charting.intro: Record measured values and distinguish what you found from what you did.

first.title: Record tooth measurements
first.text:
Use Charting to choose Grid or By tooth. Enter recorded periodontal measurements against the numbered teeth. Use Customize to choose which columns appear and how pocket measurements are entered.

Select a numbered tooth on the diagram in By tooth to open its measurements and notes together. In Grid, select tooth numbers to work with several teeth. Shift-click selects a range. Both views share the same measurements.

second.title: Document findings on Diagnosis
second.text:
Select the appropriate tooth and mark pre-treatment findings or teeth already missing. Add dental codes and short notes as needed. Use the code reference when you need to confirm a code. The toolbar labels sit below their icons. Use Comment to attach a note to a tooth, or Free comment to place a note anywhere on the diagram. The toolbar shortens Free comment to Free when space is limited.

While Comment is selected, the Comment text size choices are always visible. The diagrams in Diagnosis and Procedure show disabled editing tools after finalization. You can still zoom and toggle tooth numbers.

third.title: Document work on Procedure
third.text: Use Procedure for work performed during this visit, including completed extractions. Record narrative details in Treatment report. Keep planned procedures in your documentation until they are performed.

exam.title: Exam and anesthesia
exam.intro: Record observations and anesthetic details where they belong.

first.title: Document the exam
first.text:
Open Exam and select Normal or Abnormal for each area you assessed. Add details in Comment. Leave unassessed areas blank. Use Diagnostics below the exam findings to record non-imaging results and pending tests.

In the Exam header, choose Customize to open Oral exam in Chart settings. You can also select Oral exam from the Chart settings categories. The default layout includes six dental exam areas and Diagnostics. Select a field to edit its Field name. Use Add field to add an Exam area with status choices and a comment, or a Text field for free-form notes. Drag a field by its handle or focus the handle and use the arrow keys.

Use the remove button beside a field to take it out of the layout. Select Undo to put it back or use Add field to restore a built-in field. Recorded findings stay visible after removal. Choose Save, then check the field names and order in Exam.

Practice owners can save the shared layout. Other practice members can view the layout. If you work outside a shared practice, the layout saves to your personal chart settings.

second.title: Record anesthetics and blocks
second.text:
Open Anesthesia, enter the anesthetic drugs, and record site and volume for the blocks performed. Check sides and units against your source before finalizing. Use Add a second nerve-block set when you gave a different anesthetic separately. Record its name, strength, and site volumes in the second set.

In the Anesthesia header, choose Customize. Under Nerve blocks shown, select the built-in blocks to show. Under Additional nerve blocks, choose Add nerve block to add a named block with right and left volume fields. Under Custom anesthesia fields, choose Add field to add a field such as a note for the endotracheal tube. Choose an existing custom item to edit its name or remove it. Close Chart settings and check the fields in Anesthesia.

In the same settings, set your Preferred local anesthetic and, optionally, an Additional medication. When the visit has no anesthetic recorded, Anesthesia offers a shortcut. Check the drug names and strengths before using it. Applying the shortcut records the configured medications for that visit.

third.title: Review the recorded findings
third.text: After dictation, check the findings in Exam and the block sites and drugs in Anesthesia. Correct incomplete or uncertain entries before you finalize the dental visit.

imaging.title: Imaging and reports
imaging.intro: Manage clinical images, radiographs, and CT findings for the current visit.

first.title: Add images and review history
first.text: Use Add images to browse, drop, or paste files on the web. Where supported, DICOM files keep the original for download. In Image history, expand the row or open the earlier visit to inspect past images. The original filename appears along the bottom of a photo or radiograph when it was saved with the upload. Open the image to read the full name.

second.title: Choose report inclusion
second.text: Set each image’s type and optional tooth and description. Choose whether it appears in the clinical PDF or owner report. Use the Before or After label when it helps explain the image. Refine is in the lower corner of the text box.

third.title: Write the imaging reports
third.text:
Enter findings in Radiographic report or CT report. For other results and pending tests, open Exam and use Diagnostics. You can dictate all of these in the same dental recording. Name the modality when describing imaging and check the proposed destinations before applying them.

In the Imaging header, choose Customize to open Customize Imaging. Practice owners can change the shared report layout. Expand Radiographic report or CT report to edit its label and Starter text. For example, add headings for technique, findings, and impression.

Save the practice layout, then open Imaging in a new dental visit to check the labels and starter text. Editing the starter text in the report records it for that visit. Reports already recorded keep their text.

To change the report language or default PDF inclusion, choose Imaging and PDF settings in the customization dialog. Outside a shared practice, Customize opens those settings directly.

dictation.title: Dictation and AI review
dictation.intro: Use one recording for the dental visit and review how the findings are applied.

first.title: Start the dental recording
first.text: Choose Dictate from any tab of a dental procedure, then start recording. Allow microphone access if prompted. As you work through the visit, name tooth numbers, sides, units and imaging modalities where they matter.

second.title: Check the transcript and proposals
second.text: Clear findings can fill the matching tabs while you speak, including Exam, Anesthesia, Charting, Diagnosis and Procedure. The active tab gives context to ambiguous wording. Stop when you finish and review the transcript and chart.

third.title: Review corrections before applying
third.text:
In Charting, follow the entries in Activity as you dictate. Clear numeric findings can appear as “Charted directly,” for example when you give a tooth number and a mobility score. Select “Stop dictation” to pause the microphone. While the panel says “Dictation paused,” select “Resume” if you have more to add.

“Checking chart” starts automatically and compares the transcript with the chart. When “Chart checked” appears, look for any items under “Needs review.” In Needs review, compare proposed changes with existing values and keep the supported wording. At the end, the same recording can propose CT, other diagnostic results and discharge details. Compare the proposed sections with their evidence and select the ones to apply.

An exclamation mark in chart navigation identifies a section with findings that need review. Open that section to see the suggestions and their actions. A valid estimate can fill an empty field. If the field already has a different value, the suggestion appears alongside it. Review from the chart or from the Dictate panel. Pending findings stay with the visit when you close and reopen it.

treatment.title: Treatment reports and templates
treatment.intro: Use reusable wording and document what was performed at this visit.

first.title: Write the treatment report
first.text: Open Treatment report and enter the procedures performed, any relevant findings, and details needed for the record. Dictation uses the current section as context.

second.title: Use a saved template
second.text: Choose a named template in Saved templates. Check the populated wording before saving. The report remains editable, and Refine can suggest cleaner wording for review. Refine is in the lower corner of the text box.

third.title: Create a reusable template
third.text:
Open Manage templates, then choose + (Create template). Give the template a recognizable name and write the reusable text. Type { in the template editor to see the supported fill-in codes. Use a field like {pet} for the patient name. When you select the saved template, ToothOps fills in recorded chart values. Any unfilled codes stay in the report for you to edit.

Open Manage templates beside Saved templates to edit a template. To remove one, select it and open More options, then choose Delete.

discharge.title: Discharge and owner reports
discharge.intro: Prepare the take-home document from the recorded visit.

first.title: Record discharge instructions
first.text:
Dental recovery is selected for new visits unless your practice has chosen another default. In Discharge, choose from the available options under “Note template”. Switching templates keeps the wording you have already entered. After changing templates, expand “Fields from other templates” below the current fields to find previously entered text for fields that are outside the active template.

In Discharge, list one medication per line with the dose, how to give it, and for how long. Add home care and follow-up instructions. Check the details before sharing.

Open “Manage templates” beside the choices. Practice owners can edit any template, including Dental recovery and Standard discharge. Choose “New template” to start with the standard sections and give the template a name. Under “More options”, choose “Duplicate” to copy a template or “Set as practice default” to preselect it on new visits. Choose “Delete template” to remove it from the practice list. Keep at least one active template. Saved visits retain their layout and text. The + button creates a template, and the question mark opens the guide.

To reorder templates, drag a template by the handle beside its name. You can also focus the handle and press the Up or Down arrow key. Choose “Save” to apply the order.

Open “Add section” and use “Search sections” to find a built-in field or a reusable field under “Practice fields”. If the field you need is missing, choose “Create a field” and enter a field name. To use it in another template, select it under “Practice fields” in that template’s picker.

Expand a section and choose Field type. Use Long text or Short text for editable text, Single choice for radio buttons, or Multiple choice for checkboxes. Add and name your options before saving. Open Manage practice fields and choose Delete to remove a reusable field from the picker. Templates already using it keep the field.

Drag a field by its handle to change the order. Use the X to remove the field from the current template, or select “Undo” to put it back. Select the field name to expand its settings. To share a custom field, turn on “Include in owner report” in that template. If you use the same field in another template, set its sharing option there as well.

Use “Sample preview” to check how the sections look with fictional content. Choose “Save”, select the template for the visit, and use “Review and export” → “Record note” to check the clinical note.

To place the visit gallery, choose Images under Add section. Select the Images row to set its label and guidance. Drag it to the desired position or use the arrow keys on the handle. Removing the row hides the gallery in that template and keeps the visit’s attachments.

second.title: Draft the owner report
second.text:
In Owner report, choose a named template under Report template to use it for this visit, or choose Practice default to follow the practice’s current default. The highlighted choice is active. Scroll inside the list when there are more templates. To edit shared wording or layout, choose Manage templates. Practice owners can choose Create template in the editor, or use Template actions to set a default. Select Save templates when finished. Use Write with AI beside the wording to draft the opening summary and home care advice. Check and edit the draft before sharing. Restore generated returns a section to its saved draft. The + button creates a template, and the question mark opens the guide.

To reorder sections in the owner report editor, drag a section by its handle or focus the handle and use the arrow keys.

third.title: Preview and share
third.text: Use Preview in the Owner report heading to open the owner PDF and verify the wording and layout. To include images, select them in Imaging. Use Review and export to download or, when available, email the report after checking the recipient and document. The Owner report tab has Customize, Download PDF, and, when available, Email to owner in the bar above the preview.

export.title: Review, export, and finalize
export.intro: Check the right document before sharing and close the visit when it is complete.

first.title: Choose a document
first.text: Open Review and export for the selected visit. For a dental procedure, choose Clinical chart for the chart PDF, Owner report for the take-home PDF where enabled, or Record note for text. For a consultation, use Record note to download or copy that visit’s note.

second.title: Customize the clinical PDF
second.text: In Clinical chart, open Customize to choose colors and the sections to include, such as images, imaging reports, and Codes used. Check the preview after changing an option and download the document when ready. Discharge sections appear below the imaging reports by default. Clear the option to hide them from the printed pages. Find Customize and Download PDF next to the document tabs.

third.title: Finalize or reopen a visit
third.text: Choose Finalize and confirm to save the completed visit and make it view-only. To amend a saved visit, open it, choose Edit chart, make the change, then choose Done editing. Confirm the patient and date before applying edits.

rechecks.title: Rechecks and reminders
rechecks.intro: Record the next follow-up and monitor due visits.

first.title: Record a recheck date
first.text: In Patient, set Recheck due when a date has been agreed. Add instructions in Discharge when needed. Confirm the owner contact details if reminders will be sent.

second.title: Work through the recheck list
second.text: Open Rechecks to see scheduled follow-ups. Open the patient or earlier visit when you need the clinical context. Clear completed items when appropriate.

third.title: Set up reminders
third.text: Open Recheck reminders in practice or app settings to review the available sending options. Check the recipient and schedule before sending a reminder.

settings.title: Account and practice settings
settings.intro: Set up the chart for the team and separate personal preferences from shared settings.

first.title: Set your own preferences
first.text: Use Account to change your app language and profile. Use Chart settings, or Customize within a chart section, for chart layout, measurements, imaging, and PDF display options.

second.title: Manage shared practice settings
second.text:
Practice owners can manage branding, team access, and shared owner report templates. The practice’s client language controls client-facing defaults, including report wording.

On the web, edit the practice name in Practice settings → General. Use Save below the name field to apply the change, or Cancel to restore the current name.

third.title: Check which features are available
third.text: Some clinical sections, AI tools, and report actions depend on the practice’s settings, access, and your role. If you cannot see a tool, check that the correct practice and an editable visit are open.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.intro: Resolve common problems with saving, recording, images, or export.

first.title: A visit is not saving
first.text: Check the save indicator and your connection. Confirm the visit has a patient name and clinical content. Use the available retry or manual save action. Keep the chart open until its save status is confirmed.

second.title: The microphone or AI is unavailable
second.text: Allow microphone access in the browser or device settings, close other recording sessions, and check the connection. Open an editable chart and use Start dictation. If a result seems wrong, keep the saved value and review the transcript.

third.title: A report is missing content
third.text: Confirm the correct visit and document tab. Check the report template, PDF inclusion options, and individual image inclusion. Use Help to send feedback if the issue persists, and describe what you expected and what you saw.

account.title: Sign in and manage your account
account.intro: Set up access, recover a password, or update your profile.

first.title: Sign in or accept an invitation
first.text: Sign in with your account email. If you are creating an account, follow the confirmation link sent to your inbox. If a practice invited you, use the invitation sent to the email address you will use for ToothOps.

second.title: Recover access
second.text: Use Forgot password on the sign-in screen and follow the link in the email. If a session expires while you are charting, sign in again to resume cloud saving. Check that the correct visit is open before you continue.

third.title: Update your profile and credentials
third.text: Open Account to update your display name, email, password, or app language. Follow the confirmation shown by each section.

viewer.title: Review images and DICOM files
viewer.intro: Use the image viewer to inspect an attachment and recover its original file.

first.title: Open the viewer
first.text: Select an image in Imaging or in an earlier visit. Use the viewer controls to zoom, fit, or move around the image. Review details against the original acquisition when needed. The full filename appears at the bottom of the viewer when available.

second.title: Adjust the display
second.text: For supported original DICOM files, use Window / level to work with the original data. On desktop, hold Shift and drag horizontally to adjust window or vertically to adjust level. Use brightness and contrast when window and level are unavailable.

third.title: Download the original
third.text: Use Download original DICOM from the image actions when the original is available. If the file cannot be read, try an uncompressed DICOM or a supported image format exported from the original imaging software.

recovery.title: Saved visits, versions, and PDF import
recovery.intro: Recover a saved version or continue from a ToothOps chart PDF.

first.title: Understand save status
first.text: Check the save indicator on the active patient tab. Offline changes can stay on the device until the connection returns. If ToothOps reports a newer save from another device or teammate, compare the current chart before confirming that you want to replace those changes.

second.title: Review or restore an earlier version
second.text: Use Chart history to compare saves within the same dated visit. Select a version to see what was recorded. To restore, open the visit for editing, select Restore this version, and confirm. The pre-restore version remains in history.

third.title: Import a chart PDF
third.text: Choose Import chart PDF in the patient library and select a chart PDF previously exported by ToothOps. Confirm any prompt about the chart currently open, then verify the patient and visit date before continuing. A PDF from another source may not contain an editable ToothOps chart.

preferences.title: Customize ToothOps
preferences.intro: Find the right Customize control for chart entry, diagram defaults, report templates, or PDF output.

first.title: Find the right settings for your task
first.text:
Open Patient, Anesthesia, Charting, Diagnosis, Procedure and choose Customize in that section’s header. Chart settings opens at the matching category. In the left-hand category list, choose another area without leaving the dialog. Personal chart preferences save automatically to your account when account sync is available, or to the current browser otherwise.

For Exam, select Oral exam in Chart settings to edit the layout. In Imaging, choose Customize in the header to edit the shared layout or open Imaging and PDF settings.

In Treatment report, Manage templates beside the saved choices opens the treatment templates. In Owner report, Manage templates beside the report template choices opens the owner report templates. These editors manage reusable wording and layout for your practice, so review the selected template before changing it.

second.title: Understand each Chart settings category
second.text:
The Chart settings sidebar organizes the options by the part of the visit they affect. In Charting, for example, choose Grid or By tooth, your pocket depth mode, which measurements are visible, and what happens after you enter a score. Configure Diagnosis and Procedure shortcuts independently because they apply to different diagrams.

For fields in Patient, open Customize. In Owner details and Visit details, select the fields to show. For example, use Visit details to show a recheck date. Close Chart settings and check the fields in Patient.

Changes to field visibility or diagram display help you focus while charting. Review entered findings in the patient record before you export.

third.title: Set imaging defaults and customize exports
third.text:
In the Imaging header, choose Customize, then select Imaging and PDF settings for the imaging report language and default inclusion options. You can include images, radiographic and CT reports, and the Codes used section. The charting grid is required when diagram findings are turned off, so recorded measurements remain visible in the clinical document.

For a specific export, open Review and export, select Clinical chart, and open Customize. Choose the clinical PDF color and included sections, then inspect the preview. For an owner handout, use the Owner report template and choose which individual images to include from Imaging. Changing the clinical PDF color does not select an owner report template.

team.title: Practice setup and team access
team.intro: Manage shared branding, colleagues, and report templates.

first.title: Set up practice branding
first.text: Open Practice settings to update the practice name and logo as allowed by your role. Preview a PDF to verify how the practice details appear. Set the client language for default text shown to owners.

second.title: Invite and manage colleagues
second.text: Open Team in Practice settings. Invite colleagues using the email address they will sign in with. Check pending invitations and use the available resend or cancel action. A practice owner can manage member access and ownership.

third.title: Manage shared templates
third.text: Open Templates in Practice settings, or Customize beside the relevant report. Practice owners can manage owner report layouts, wording, and the practice default. When editing an existing template, preview the sample before saving changes.

billing.title: Subscription and billing
billing.intro: Find the subscription and payment controls for your practice.

first.title: Find your subscription
first.text: In ToothOps on the web, open Practice settings, then Billing. The page shows the available subscription information for your practice. Ask the practice owner for billing changes if you do not have access.

second.title: Manage payments and invoices
second.text: When Manage billing is available, use it to open the Stripe portal. View invoices, change the payment method, or manage your subscription from the portal. Check that you are managing the intended practice.

third.title: Resolve an access issue
third.text: If the practice has a billing or access notice, follow the action shown on the web. Use Help to reach support when a payment or subscription status looks incorrect.

help-tools.title: Get help and see what changed
help-tools.intro: Use the walkthrough, release notes, and feedback tools.

first.title: Open the walkthrough
first.text: Choose Getting started from Help. The walkthrough points out the controls in the app and can be opened again as needed. On narrow screens, open the dropdown beside your practice name or logo to find these tools.

second.title: Review recent changes
second.text: Open What’s new from Help to review recent changes. For a new workflow, open its guide in the Help Center.

third.title: Send useful feedback
third.text: Use Send feedback from Help when you encounter a problem or have an idea. Describe what you were doing, what happened, and what you expected. Remove patient or owner information before attaching a screenshot.

by-number.title: Chart by tooth number
by-number.intro: Use the numbered diagram to document measurements, diagnosis, and procedure notes for one tooth at a time.

first.title: Open By tooth and select a number
first.text:
Open the Charting section and select By tooth beside Grid. Select the numbered tooth on the diagram. The editor heading shows the Triadan number and tooth name, so you can check your selection before entering a finding. For example, 108 is the upper right fourth premolar on the adult canine diagram. The numbers follow the species and dentition selected in Patient.

If the diagram is collapsed in a narrow browser window, select Tooth map, choose a quadrant, and then select the number. Use the previous or next tooth buttons to move through the mouth without reopening the map.

second.title: Record findings, notes, and extraction status
second.text:
Enter the recorded measurements in Findings. A pocket depth can be a single reading, one reading per root, or six site-specific readings. Open Customize in Charting to choose the pocket depth mode and the measurements you want to see. Mark Missing (before this visit) only when the tooth was already missing.

Use Diagnosis note and any configured quick codes for what you found, and Procedure note for what you did. Use Plan to extract for intended work. When the extraction has happened, mark it extracted. The diagram key distinguishes recorded findings, planned extraction, completed extraction, and missing teeth.

third.title: Switch views or dictate a numbered finding
third.text:
Grid and By tooth edit the same chart. Measurements you enter in the numbered editor also appear in Grid. Diagnosis and Procedure notes and marks appear on their respective diagrams. You can switch views at any point to check your work.

To dictate, stay in Charting, choose Dictate, and start recording. Say the full number and the finding, for example, “108, distal pocket five millimetres.” Check the result against the intended tooth and the available pocket fields. If a suggested change conflicts with a recorded value, review it before applying.

consultation.title: Document a consultation
consultation.intro: Capture and review a note inside the patient’s visit.

first.title: Choose a template
first.text: From the patient, choose New visit. If Consultation is available, select it and choose Start visit. Under Note template, pick one of the visible choices. Check the highlighted choice and section order. Changing templates keeps the text you entered.

second.title: Enter or dictate the visit
second.text:
Use Dental consultation for a pre-procedure visit. In Awake oral examination, record visible findings and what you could not assess. Record relevant risks in Pre-anesthetic considerations. Use Client discussion and decisions to document options, estimates, consent status, and care that is deferred or still pending. Record home dental care and the agreed follow-up in their own sections. If a template provides Suggested text, review it and choose Use suggested text only when it applies to this visit.

Record the reason for the visit, history, assessment and plan. If dictation is available, compare the proposed sections with their evidence before applying them. To revisit a transcript, open Saved transcripts and select the recording date. Record vital signs, examination and diagnostics under their own fields when those findings were documented. Leave fields blank when you have no findings to enter. Below Plan and the other note fields, open Images and choose Add images. Select files, or drop or paste them into the visit. Wait for thumbnails to appear and open one to check it. Images stay attached to this visit and do not appear in the standalone note PDF. Use Current medications for reported use, Medications given during this visit for doses actually given, and Medication changes and prescriptions for the plan. During dictation, say which category each medication belongs to and review the quoted evidence before applying. In Current medications, open Previous medication list to see the most recent earlier consultation and any recorded changes. Check what is still current, then choose Copy to current medications if the field is empty. Use Look up a drug to enter a drug name and open the DailyMed label search. Select Search labels, then choose the exact veterinary product. Use Open full label on DailyMed to verify the strength, directions and warnings.

third.title: Review the note
third.text: Choose Review clinical record to open the record note for this visit. Confirm that the documented findings are present and in the expected order before transferring the note.

consultation-templates.title: Customize consultation templates
consultation-templates.intro: Set a consistent note order for your practice.

first.title: Start from an existing template
first.text:
Open Manage templates in Consultation. Practice owners can select and edit any template, including Dental consultation, General SOAP, and Recheck. Choose New template to start from the dental layout, or More options → Duplicate to copy the selected template. The + button creates a template, and the question mark opens the guide.

In More options, choose Create from a sample note to paste a de-identified example. Use Markdown headings or labels followed by a colon. Select Create template, then review the imported headings. The note body stays out of the template.

second.title: Arrange and preview sections
second.text:
Open “Add section” and use “Search sections” to find a built-in field or a reusable field under “Practice fields”. If the field you need is missing, choose “Create a field” and enter a field name. To use it in another template, select it under “Practice fields” in that template’s picker.

Expand a section and choose Field type. Use Long text or Short text for editable text, Single choice for radio buttons, or Multiple choice for checkboxes. Add and name your options before saving. Open Manage practice fields and choose Delete to remove a reusable field from the picker. Templates already using it keep the field.

Select a field name to change its section label, guidance, example wording, suggested text, output format, or subsection setting. Open “Dictation settings” to set writing instructions and the level of detail. Use suggested text only after confirming it applies to the current visit. Drag a field by its handle to change the order. Use the X to remove the field from the current template, or select “Undo” to put it back.

Enter a template name. Open “Sample preview” to check the field order with fictional visit details, then select it again to return to editing.

After changing templates, expand “Fields from other templates” below the current fields to find previously entered text for fields that are outside the active template.

To place the visit gallery, choose Images under Add section. Select the Images row to set its label and guidance. Drag it to the desired position or use the arrow keys on the handle. Removing the row hides the gallery in that template and keeps the visit’s attachments.

third.title: Save, reorder, or delete templates
third.text: Drag a template by the handle beside its name or focus the handle and press the Up or Down arrow key. In More options, choose Set as practice default for new visits or Delete template to remove it from the list. Keep at least one template. Choose Save to apply the changes. Saved visits keep their selected layout.

consultation-transfer.title: Review and transfer a consultation note
consultation-transfer.intro: Check the clinical record before downloading, copying or sending it.

first.title: Open the record note
first.text: In Consultation, choose Review clinical record. The record note opens with the visit findings. Review the text and edit the wording if the visit is open for editing.

second.title: Check for updated findings
second.text: If a notice says the chart changed after the note was edited, compare the note with the current visit. Keep any manual wording you need before selecting Rebuild from chart, which replaces the edited note with the current chart content.

third.title: Download, copy or send
third.text: Select Download PDF to save a standalone PDF of the consultation, including any edits in Record note. Use Copy to paste the note into the intended record, or use the built-in transfer when available. Confirm the patient, visit date and content at the destination.
